fixtures.prompt: Explain to our engineering team how to migrate from one shared OAuth credential to per-workspace OAuth. Cover the trust boundary, rollout stages, failure recovery, observability, and the tradeoffs in enough detail for us to review the design in Slack.

Teach a newer engineer how backpressure should work in our asynchronous job queue. Include admission, bounded buffering, retries, idempotency, overload behavior, and concrete examples of what operators should see.

Draft a thoughtful incident follow-up for customers after a two-hour delay in Slack responses. It should acknowledge impact, explain the failure without hand-waving, describe the repair and prevention work, and set expectations for the next update.

Write a detailed internal rollout announcement for a new workspace permissions model. Include why it is changing, what members and admins will experience, the rollout sequence, rollback criteria, and where to report confusing behavior.

Analyze the product and engineering tradeoffs between terminal-only Slack answers and selectively progressive answers. Consider perceived latency, answer stability, correction risk, accessibility, provider differences, and operational complexity, then recommend a policy.

Compare three onboarding models for a Slack agent: configure everything before first use, progressively disclose setup after connection, or begin with a guided first task. Evaluate time to value, recovery, user comprehension, and implementation risk.
Confirm in one short sentence that the migration checklist is complete.
Reply only with a brief acknowledgement that you understand.
Return only valid JSON with keys status, owner, and retryable. Use complete, platform, and false as their values. Do not add prose or a code fence.
Return only a two-column Markdown table mapping dev to development, stg to staging, and prod to production.
Correction: in your prior answer, change the retry limit from five to three and the timeout from 60 seconds to 45 seconds. Restate only the corrected sentence.
Your last reply called the feature Smart Streams. Correct it to Progressive Answers and give me the corrected one-line heading only.
Check the current production deployment status and tell me whether the latest release is healthy. Use the deployment tools available to you before answering.
Inspect the repository and tell me the exact file and line where the Slack retry limit is configured. Do not guess; look it up before answering.
Explain in two or three paragraphs why an idempotency key is useful for sending Slack messages.
Give me a short explanation of the rollout risk followed by a five-item checklist for mitigating it.
Write a concise decision note comparing server-sent events and polling for a status panel, with a recommendation.
What are the two most important risks of progressively revealing an AI answer, and how would you mitigate each one?
